target_customer: In-house legal and business teams at mid-size and large companies that create and manage contracts
problem: Companies run contracts through email and documents, which is slow and hard to track; many build their own tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for contract lifecycle management

founders.name: Jason Boehmig
founders.background_notes: Spent two years as a corporate attorney at Fenwick & West (Fortune, 2017). Company about page calls him an attorney.

founders.name: Cai GoGwilt
founders.background_notes: Software engineer at Palantir (Fortune, 2017). Company about page spells the surname differently; Fortune spelling used.

technical_complexity.rationale: Workflow engine, document editing and integrations with Salesforce and other systems were standard but broad engineering; later AI features added difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Once contracts and approval workflows live in the platform it is costly to change, but incumbents and many rivals offered similar workflows.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were not seen buying it. Fortune named Apttus as a rival in 2017; Ironclad later raised through 2022 and acquired clickwrap vendor PactSafe in 2021.

market_need_then: Fortune reported in 2017 that many companies built their own contract systems from databases and content management software, showing demand and pain. It was quietly rolled out at GoFundMe, Glassdoor and HotelTonight.

branding.domain_note: Began as Ironclad.ai per company about page; later uses ironcladapp.com. Other companies share the name (for example Ironclad Performance Wear).

identity.logo: Icon mark representing two parties coming together with Ironclad at the center (kept in the 2019 redesign)
identity.visual_style: Rebuilt brand platform in 2019 to feel premium and scalable

branding.brand_signature: The Ironclad name and two-parties icon mark

rebrands.from: Original five day logo and identity
rebrands.why: Team felt the first brand was not scalable or premium (designer account)

branding.community_and_virality: Hosts Apex, a summit for in-house legal leaders, launched 2019 (company about page).

brand_strength.rationale: Strong B2B presence with a leader recognition from Gartner and customers such as Salesforce and L'Oreal, but the name is shared by unrelated companies and no evidence shows it as a growth driver.

outcome_analysis: Ironclad followed a steady venture path: $8M Series A in 2017, Series B and C in 2019, a roughly $100M Series D in 2021 and a $150M Series E in January 2022 at a reported $3.2B valuation. It passed $200M in ARR by early 2026 and named Dan Springer CEO in 2025. A strong enterprise sales motion in a large category explains the outcome; no exit has happened.
notes: Series B date conflicts: Wikipedia says 2018, Multiples says January 2019; recorded as 2019 with Pulse 2 as source (amount from that outlet) and the month unknown. Series D amount and Series E details come from Wikipedia and aggregators (Clay, Multiples); Series D date is given as 2021 by the company, 2020 by CB Insights. Series E valuation of $3.2B comes from a Forbes headline cited on the YC page. Crunchbase News says total funding was $84M at September 2019. Education not found. Competitor Apttus is named in a 2017 Fortune article, two years after the batch, so it is not listed as of founding; Clio is a later-year peer. Search for 2015 era competitors returned only current roundups.
